title: NFL Week 10 fantasy football rankings: Where do all of the traded players rank?
content:
We wanted more from the NFL trade deadline — new team for Jonathan Taylor, anyone? Nevertheless, we did get some action, and action that affects the Week 10 fantasy football rankings. Kirk Cousins has a ripple effect; Josh Downs and Keenan Allen step into top-two receiving roles; and well, there wasn’t much else outside of even more injuries to discuss! I break it all down with the start-or-sit decisions we have pending, plus a fun ranks where I want your input.

If you haven’t seen this yet, here’s how The Fantasy Concierge works: Type in the names of up to five players, select your scoring format and the position(s) you want to compare, and click the analyze button to see who I’d recommend starting this week, along with recent related coverage from The Athletic’s NFL and Fantasy teams.

* Ranks need context. This year, each skill position will still have notes for potential changes based on news, injuries, weather, etc. Rankings are updated all week and always before kickoff on game day (except Monday, because they’re locked). Tiers are Disney afternoon-cartoons style because it was the best time ever.

BYES: Bears, Broncos, Buccaneers, Eagles

* Referenced stats are since Week 4 to account for recency (changes, etc.)

So, this one is a bit selfish in that I’m also looking for suggestions outside of what a Google search tells me. I want to hear from the people! Being an adult who enjoys “couples parties” with food and games seems rare — maybe I just need more friends. Obviously, I went through the Cards Against Humanity phase like everyone, and we’ll still break it out … with the right group (and having thrown away a few over-the-top cards — there is a line at some point). This list includes that, but it’s only based on my/our experience, and I feel like this has untapped potential … with your help!

10. Taboo: More of a classic at this point, as you get your team to guess a word without using the five words on the card. It has an annoying buzzer that will get abused by opponents … and kids if they’re around.
9. Sorry What?!: There is a Cards Against Humanity-like version and family version, but it’s essentially how good of a lip-reader you are.
8. Guesstures: It’s charades with added stress. You act out as many cards as you can before the timer drops the card inside. Who doesn’t want charades with added anxiety?
7. Taco Cat Goat Cheese Pizza: This can get dangerous from a physicality standpoint. Don’t put drinks on the table. This is “Spit” taken up a few notches.
6. Decrypto: You need people invested, so maybe it’s not for everyone, as it’s team-based where you try to guess the opposing team’s code.
5. Catchphrase: Beware of people throwing this disk at you. You sit with every player next to someone from the opposing team, and you try to get your team to guess the word. The timer ticks down, and if you’re holding it when it goes off, the other team scores. There’s nothing like the argument over who was actually holding it.
4. Cards Against Humanity: You know the deal. This is not something you play with family.
3. Monikers: We tried this after seeing recommendations for this as a “better version” of Codenames (I never played that, so don’t kill the messenger). You have three rounds of getting people to guess the “celebrity” by describing the card, using only one word, and then with charades.
2. Telestrations: Only discovered it thanks to Nicole, but take Pictionary and smash it together with the telephone game, and laugh your tails off at the results.
1. Jackbox: Many of our favorites are on here, and there is a plethora of games at this point (12 party packs). Drawful is arguably the best, but Fibbage, Quiplash, Fakin’ It and Trivia Murder Party make our favorites list and regular rotation. Fibbage and Quiplash rely a bit on quick humor from the players, especially Quiplash, so take note. I could have done a top 10 of Jackbox games.

(Hey, listen! 🧚 It’s mine 👀)
